pbContract: Record create/update extracts every upload under field, +field, field+ names before saving.
pgImplementation: A multipart batch uses a requests JSON part and named file parts referenced through $file. It stages all bytes, then commits record changes and attachment metadata in one PostgreSQL transaction.
gap: Complete atomic batch capability with a different request protocol; the standalone upload endpoint accepts one file part.

pbContract: MaxSelect <=1 means one file; larger values allow multiple files; Required requires at least one. PocketBase has no FileField minSelect.
pgImplementation: Field MaximumCount and Required are checked under a per-record/field advisory lock. Both staged batch removals and standalone deletion reject an empty required field.

pbContract: Default maxSize is 5 MiB; field MIME list is optional; configured MIME types are checked by detected file type.
pgImplementation: Enforces field and global size/type ceilings, declared size and SHA-256, MIME sniffing and image pixel limits. Global maximum is 100 MiB and the default MIME list is restrictive.
gap: Intentional additional global budgets and MIME declaration checks; empty configuration is not PocketBase's allow-any MIME mode.

pbContract: Record file setters support replace, append field+, prepend +field and filename removal field-. Upload failure cleans previously uploaded files; successful saves delete detached objects.
pgImplementation: Batch field modifiers now support replace/append/prepend/remove and preserve order. Metadata changes share the record transaction; physical deletion is deferred through durable object GC.
gap: The old comparison's unsupported-modifier claim is stale. Physical deletion timing differs intentionally; see FIL-19 for the separate standalone malformed-upload edge.

pbContract: Protected files evaluate the collection view rule using auth derived from a file token. An invalid/missing token supplies nil auth, which may still pass an explicitly public view rule. Protected defaults false.
pgImplementation: Fields default protected; explicit protected=false enables the public file-ID URL. Authenticated access checks current record/field policy; hiding or protecting a field revokes access through existing URLs/tokens.
gap: Secure default and authenticated-token policy intentionally differ from PocketBase; do not claim identical public/protected semantics.

pbContract: GET /api/files/{collection name or ID}/{recordId}/{filename} resolves a record file and supplies its download filename.
pgImplementation: Exposes UUID file-ID URLs and Content-Disposition filenames, plus file metadata/publicUrl. Authenticated and public paths differ.
gap: URL identity and wire format differ. Range/conditional/inline behavior is separately missing in FIL-14.

pbContract: POST /api/files/token creates an auth-record file token; URL token identifies that auth record, which is then checked against each file's view rule.
pgImplementation: Per-file token includes principal ID/kind, variant and expiry; minting and opening reauthorize current policy. TTL defaults 5 minutes, capped at 15. The private HTTP URL also needs caller authentication.
gap: Token-only links suitable for unauthenticated image elements are not the private PgBase contract; use the SDK/authenticated route or explicitly public fields.

pbContract: Supports centered WxH, top/bottom crop, fit and zero-axis aspect-preserving resize.
pgImplementation: Parses the same principal size modes as variant values, with explicit declared field variants and stricter dimension/pixel/byte bounds. Rendering uses nearest-neighbor sampling.
gap: Request parameter is variant, not thumb. No pixel-identical rendering claim: PocketBase uses imaging.Linear; current PgBase crop test mainly checks dimensions.

pbContract: Record HTTP thumbnails accept PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP. Generic CreateThumb also understands TIFF/BMP; output follows supported encoder or falls back to PNG.
pgImplementation: Record transforms decode PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP. PNG remains PNG; JPEG/GIF/WebP become JPEG, using a single frame. GIF/WebP require explicit allowed MIME configuration.
gap: Output encoding/transparency differs intentionally. Generic TIFF/BMP transforms are not implemented; EXIF orientation is a separate missing behavior in FIL-15.

pbContract: Caches thumbnails by path; singleflight deduplicates one key and a configurable semaphore bounds simultaneous generation and wait.
pgImplementation: Caches variant receipts and bytes; PostgreSQL advisory locks serialize generation across processes; publication fencing and reference-aware cleanup handle failed metadata commits.
gap: Cross-process DB locking replaces local singleflight; PocketBase's PB_THUMBS_MAX_WORKERS/MAX_WAIT knobs are not exposed.

pbContract: Local filesystem stores objects under its configured root and supports read/write/delete operations.
pgImplementation: Validated physical object keys stay under a configured root. Writes use a same-directory temporary file then rename; canceled writes remove temporary files and delete is idempotent.
gap: Opaque object keys and metadata-backed publication differ from PocketBase's record-directory layout; neither cited test establishes power-loss durability.

pbContract: NewFilesystem selects local or S3 using runtime app settings including endpoint, bucket, region, credentials and path style.
pgImplementation: Configured S3 backend supports put/open/delete; runtime settings redact/encrypt credentials, test connectivity, rotate credentials and fence storage cutovers. Location changes with existing inventory require migration.
gap: Configured storage support is complete within the stricter migration contract. This does not establish arbitrary $filesystem.s3(...) targets; see FIL-17.

pbContract: System exposes local/S3 selection, readers/writers, copy, complete List, DeletePrefix, Serve, CreateThumb and context control.
pgImplementation: Namespace-scoped extension object storage supports immutable versions, transactional publication, streaming, pagination, copy/delete and a JS System-shaped facade. Some facade methods do not implement the PB contract.
gap: $filesystem.s3 ignores its arguments; System.list truncates at 100; setContext is a no-op. DeletePrefix itself paginates all keys, then deletes serially and stops at the first error rather than returning PB's collected errors.

pbContract: GET /api/realtime returns text/event-stream, no-store, X-Accel-Buffering:no, and a PB_CONNECT event containing clientId.
pgImplementation: The multiplex route exposes the same endpoint, headers and connect envelope.
gap: This narrow row does not assert connection lifetime or reconnect-ID equivalence; see RT-07.

pbContract: POST replaces a client's subscriptions; empty list unsubscribes all; maximum 1000 topics; validates originating IP and permits guest-to-auth upgrade only.
pgImplementation: POST performs atomic subscription replacement under a delivery mutex, validates client/IP/principal, permits empty lists and preserves cursors for unchanged subscriptions.
gap: PgBase validates collection access/options at subscription time, rejects duplicate/empty entries and requires JSON; PocketBase stores generic topic strings and authenticates at delivery.

pbContract: Subscriptions are arbitrary strings; application code can send a named message through the subscriptions broker, including names unrelated to collections.
pgImplementation: Custom topics use a reserved @ namespace; PublishApplication reversibly encodes arbitrary bounded UTF-8 topics. An exact-match broker delivers JSON payloads with bounded queues.
gap: Static lifecycle defect: replace skips collection validation for application topics, but the 1-second delivery loop does not skip them and calls ReadFor with an empty collection. The real reader rejects it, producing PB_ERROR and disconnect. The existing custom-topic test publishes immediately and uses a stub; it does not cover this tick.

pbContract: Connect is public; subscribe may associate a guest or auth record, including superusers. PocketBase has no PgBase service principal type.
pgImplementation: Optional admission supports guest, user bearer, administrator cookie and scoped service bearer; records are checked under the principal's current rules/scopes.
gap: Administrator credential protocol differs and service principals are a PgBase extension.

pbContract: Each topic carries options.query and options.headers; record topics use ViewRule, collection topics ListRule. Filter, expand, fields and enrichment apply before sending; delete delivery is prepared before deletion.
pgImplementation: Reads committed events under current ACLs, filters scalar fields and projects output. Relation filters query the current record; expand is fetched for non-delete events.
gap: Relation-filtered delete events are explicitly skipped and deleted records never expand. List AND view rules are combined for every topic. PB options.headers/custom query context are unsupported; see RT-08/09.

pbContract: Record messages use the subscription string as SSE event name and {action,record} as data; SSE id is the client ID.
pgImplementation: Multiplex messages use the same action/record envelope and subscription event name, but numeric durable delivery IDs. The legacy per-collection endpoint has its own record/cursor envelopes.
gap: Envelope shape matches on the multiplex route; field enrichment and ID/replay semantics do not fully match.

pbContract: Disables server write deadline; defaults to 5-minute idle and 30-minute maximum lifetime. Reconnect creates a fresh client and requires subscription resubmission; no durable replay is promised.
pgImplementation: Legacy stream has a 30-minute context, refreshed write deadlines and durable cursor events. Multiplex stream polls each second, retains per-topic cursors and accepts numeric Last-Event-ID.
gap: Multiplex never clears the production 30-second WriteTimeout or implements PB idle/max timers. PB_CONNECT writes a UUID SSE id that its numeric reconnect parser rejects before the first record event. Expired multiplex cursors become generic PB_ERROR on polling. Existing legacy replay tests do not prove multiplex recovery.

pbContract: Record downloads call System.Serve, which uses http.ServeContent for Range and conditional requests, serves allowed media inline and accepts download=true to force attachment.
pgImplementation: Record file handlers copy the whole stream using io.Copy, set no-store and always use attachment disposition. Query validation rejects download.
gap: No partial-content/conditional behavior or inline-versus-download toggle on record files. Extension System.serve has a separate implementation and must not be used as evidence for these routes.

pbContract: CreateThumb decodes with imaging.AutoOrientation(true), then resizes the oriented image.
pgImplementation: Decodes standard image pixels and resamples them without processing EXIF orientation.
gap: Phone JPEGs whose display orientation is stored in EXIF can produce rotated thumbnails. No PgBase orientation fixture was found/read; no runtime reproduction was performed.

pbContract: 100x100 is allowed independently of configured thumbs. Invalid/unconfigured sizes, unsupported formats or generation failure fall back to the original and expose ThumbError to the download hook.
pgImplementation: Open requires a permitted variant and propagates transform/open errors. The legacy thumbnail variant is configured separately; arbitrary 100x100 is not automatically permitted.
gap: PocketBase-compatible fallback and implicit 100x100 behavior are absent. This affects old file URLs that rely on fallback rather than errors.

pbContract: NewS3 constructs a filesystem for the supplied bucket, region, endpoint, credentials and path-style flag.
pgImplementation: The JS s3 function accepts those arguments but returns objectSystem() without using any of them. Operations use the configured namespace-backed object store.
gap: Calling the method with another target does not access that target and can instead affect current configured storage. Existing on-S3 tests verify configured backend operation, not argument handling.

pbContract: System.List iterates until EOF and returns every matching object.
pgImplementation: Go ExtensionObjects.List and top-level $filesystem.list expose pagination; System.list requests only the first 100 and returns the object array without nextCursor.
gap: The System-shaped method silently truncates inventories above 100 objects. DeletePrefix is a separate host path that does paginate; this finding does not allege its 100-object truncation.

feature: 추가: 잘못된 standalone multipart upload의 publication 원자성
pbContract: Record request parsing gathers multipart files before record saving; FileField interceptors clean up uploaded bytes on execution failure.
pgImplementation: Standalone file upload publishes through service.Upload before checking that the multipart body has reached EOF. An extra/malformed part triggers compensating Delete whose error is ignored.
gap: A deletion veto or changed authorization can leave a published attachment despite a rejected malformed request. This is a source-derived failure path, not a reproduced failure, and does not invalidate the separate atomic batch implementation.

feature: 추가: record topic은 viewRule, collection topic은 listRule
pbContract: The subscription rule map selects ViewRule for collection/recordId and ListRule for collection/* or collection.
pgImplementation: eventQuery compiles List AND View regardless of request.PublicID/RecordID.
gap: A record with a public/allowed view rule but locked list rule cannot emit to its record topic; a collection subscription can also be stricter than PB when only list allows access. No test covering distinct list/view permission combinations was found in the cited realtime tests.

feature: 추가: subscription options의 query·headers request context
pbContract: Client.Subscribe parses options={query:{...},headers:{...}}, normalizes header names and supplies both maps to realtime access checks.
pgImplementation: Topic parser permits only direct filter,expand,fields query keys. Delivery uses the connection HTTP request's rule context.
gap: PB SDK subscription options/header-dependent rules cannot be represented per topic. Direct filter/expand/fields alone do not establish equivalent request context.

feature: 추가: durable replay와 multiplex 전역 cursor 순서
pbContract: PocketBase sends live client-channel messages with client IDs and does not provide a durable ordered replay cursor.
pgImplementation: PgBase adds a durable outbox, fenced delivery sequence and 24-hour retention. Database readers order each topic separately; multiplex emits each subscription's whole batch before proceeding to the next.
gap: Added PgBase capability has an unverified global resume guarantee: e.g. first topic emits seq20 before second topic's pending seq10; disconnect at20 and reconnect with one shared cursor can skip10. Conversely later smaller IDs can replay already delivered higher events. DB single-topic ordering tests do not cover this multiplex case.

feature: 추가: 인증 해제 후 연결·재인증 semantics
pbContract: Auth-record deletion/token-key/collection-secret change clears client auth but leaves the socket active; subsequent subscribe can authenticate again.
pgImplementation: Multiplex revalidates its credential each polling tick and disconnects on loss; reconnect obtains a fresh client. Broker enqueue also checks credentials.
gap: Intentional disconnect rather than downgrade-to-guest. Authorization is checked before broker enqueue, not again in the custom-message write branch; do not infer a stronger immediate post-revocation wire guarantee from the enqueue-only test.

feature: 추가: collection ID alias로 realtime 구독
pbContract: Record broadcast matches both collection name and collection ID topic prefixes.
pgImplementation: ReadFor looks up collections WHERE name=$1 and the topic parser passes the raw first segment through.
gap: UUID collection IDs are not resolved as collection aliases even though PB accepts IDs. Exact text record identity tests exercise record identity, not collection aliases.

pbContract: Before serialization, superusers explicitly unhide collection fields; auth owner/superuser/manager email visibility rules and enrich hooks are applied.
pgImplementation: Administrator bypasses event ACL and hidden-field projection validation, but publicSnapshot unconditionally removes every hidden field before any output projection.
gap: Administrator subscribers cannot receive hidden fields like PB superusers; accepting a requested hidden field in validation does not restore it in the payload. Auth-record-specific enrich parity also is not established by the snapshot tests.
